title: Unawareness of data sharing implications
description: Homeowner registers account and enrolls cameras/sensors without full awareness of what personal data (identity, device details, location) is being shared with the Home Hub and how it will be used or stored.
assumptions: Homeowner may not read privacy policy or understand sensor data collection scope.

title: Disclosure of personal and device data
description: Home Hub receives and potentially stores identifiable information about the homeowner and enrolled cameras/sensors, leading to disclosure risks if not properly protected.
assumptions: Registration involves sending account details and sensor metadata.

title: Linkability via registration metadata
description: The data flow from homeowner to Home Hub during registration can link the external entity identity to specific devices and usage patterns through metadata or timing.
assumptions: Flow includes device enrollment which associates homeowner with sensors.
uncertainty_note: Context mapping confirms ExternalEntity->Process allows L at fl, but specific tree node is inferred.

title: Detectability of guest presence via access code entry
description: An observer of the communication flow or side-effects at the Home Hub can detect the existence and participation of a guest user by seeing the temporary access code being entered and processed, without needing the code data itself.
assumptions: The entry action produces observable side-effects or communication as per LINDDUN Detecting definition.

title: Guest unawareness of access logging
description: The guest user may be unaware that entering the temporary code at the Home Hub results in their access event being recorded or processed by the system, leading to unawareness of data processing.
assumptions: The Home Hub processes and potentially stores access logs from the code entry.
uncertainty_note: Based on typical smart home hub behavior; context does not specify logging.

title: Disclosure of sensitive home activity data
description: Local Event Log stores motion/door/sensor events that can reveal detailed inhabitant routines, presence, and behaviors when accessed or breached.
assumptions: Events include timestamps and sensor types sufficient to infer private activities.

title: Linkability of sensor events over time
description: Home Hub writes sequential events enabling linkage of activities to specific times or patterns, facilitating profiling even in a local log.
assumptions: Multiple events from the same sensors can be correlated by observers with log access.
uncertainty_note: Context suggests local storage but correlation risk remains if log is exported or accessed.

title: Detectability of event logging activity
description: The write operation to the log may expose metadata about ongoing sensor activity or system usage patterns.
assumptions: Flow metadata (e.g., write frequency) could leak information about home state.

title: Disclosure of personal video data
description: Cloud Video Storage receives and stores recorded camera clips which may contain identifiable images of individuals and their activities, leading to potential privacy breaches if access controls fail or data is accessed without authorization.

title: Identifiability of individuals in uploaded clips
description: The Home Hub shares video clips that can directly identify people and their behaviors within the home environment to the cloud service.

title: Linkability through upload metadata
description: Metadata about the data flow (e.g., timing, volume, endpoints) can link the Home Hub user account to specific video storage activities and patterns.

title: Motion alert data excessively exposed during transit to backend
description: The Home Hub forwards a real-time motion alert containing personal activity data (e.g., presence or movement in the home) to the Mobile App Backend. This transfer across the system boundary discloses personal data to additional parties/processes, violating the minimality principle as the data may be exposed more broadly than strictly required for the alert functionality.
assumptions: The motion alert qualifies as personal data under LINDDUN; the backend is a distinct process that may involve further storage or sharing.
uncertainty_note: Context directly supports Dd.4 for exposure; exact contents of 'motion alert' inferred from typical smart-home scenarios but not explicitly detailed in flow description.

title: Detectability of motion notifications via traffic analysis
description: An observer of the data flow (e.g., network provider or attacker) can detect push notifications being sent to the homeowner, revealing patterns of home activity or occupancy without needing to read the content.
assumptions: The notification channel uses observable metadata or timing that can be monitored.

title: Disclosure of home security events on recipient device
description: Notifications received on the homeowner's phone may be visible on the lock screen or to anyone accessing the device, disclosing sensitive information about motion events at the home.
assumptions: Notifications are not configured with privacy protections like hidden content on lock screen.

title: Linkability of motion events to specific homeowner identity
description: The backend process links detected motion data directly to the homeowner's account and device for targeted notification delivery, enabling profiling of user behavior.
assumptions: User account ties the notification to a persistent identity.

title: Disclosure via analytics sharing
description: Mobile app backend shares aggregated device-usage analytics with external cloud vendor, risking unintended disclosure of usage patterns if aggregation is insufficient or re-identification occurs.
assumptions: Aggregation may not fully prevent inference attacks on device usage data.
uncertainty_note: Depends on exact aggregation method and data fields shared; context does not specify details.

title: Linkability through analytics flow metadata
description: The data flow to the cloud analytics vendor enables linkability of the mobile app's usage patterns to the specific vendor via traffic analysis or flow metadata.

title: User unawareness of vendor processing
description: Cloud analytics vendor receives and processes the analytics data without end-users being fully aware of how their (aggregated) device usage is being analyzed or monetized by a third party.
uncertainty_note: Assumes lack of transparent privacy notices in the app regarding this sharing.

title: Violation of storage limitation principle upon retrieval
description: The mobile app backend (P2) retrieves the video clip and may retain it (e.g. in cache or logs) longer than strictly necessary for the homeowner playback session, violating the storage limitation principle for personal data.
assumptions: Backend may temporarily persist the clip beyond immediate playback needs
uncertainty_note: Context provides the Nc.1.1.4 node; applicability depends on whether P2 performs any storage after receipt, which is plausible but not explicitly stated in flow description
